version_notes: v1.2.2 (2026-10-20): gate fix (bundled copy, re-synced byte-identical from resume-tailor 1.1.5) - verify_no_fabrication.py: a capital letter inside a word was read as the start of a new proper noun, so "iOS" gave "OS" and "vCard" gave "Card": fragments the source never has, flagged as new (found finalizing the owner's resume, 2026-10-20). Candidates are now whole words: a lowercase-first word with an inner capital (iOS, vCard, eBay, iPhone) is checked as a whole and is never skipped as a sentence start; its hyphen parts are still checked one by one, so "non-GAAP" still gives "GAAP" and "mid-May" stays quiet. v1.2.1 (2026-10-20): gate fix (bundled copy, re-synced byte-identical from resume-tailor 1.1.4) - verify_no_fabrication.py, DOCX-shaped text (python-docx paragraph text: no bullet markers, headings are plain Title Case lines). (1) A new Title Case heading ("Earlier Experience") was not reported; only markdown and ALL CAPS headings were. A short Title Case line (1-5 words, optional colon) with a resume-section word (Experience, Education, Skills, ...) now counts as a heading, and is new only if no source line has the same text in any case. Job-title, employer and skill lines are not headings; a heading with no section word is still missed. (2) new_bullets counted only lines that start with a marker, so a new markerless bullet was never counted. When either document has no markers, every non-blank line under a heading now counts in both; lines before the first heading do not, so a headingless letter or claims list stays quiet. Found by the owner's resume reassessment (2026-10-20). v1.2.0 (2026-10-20): Description only (owner-approved 2026-10-20). Signal: after cover-letter 1.2.0, the "make me sound like I know Looker" interview ask loaded interview-prep 0/12 in a family-only install (3/3 before); reverting only cover-letter restored it to 11/12. The description now claims the ask to sound experienced in a skill the user lacks in an interview, and says to load the skill rather than answer or refuse from general knowledge. Draft probe: case 2 12/12; joint sweep 18/18 (+3/3 more on cases 2, 3). Evidence: docs/evals/trigger-2026-10-18-interview-prep-case2/. Joint family-only sweep with all four 2026-10-20 description changes applied together: all 40 outcome-eval turn-1 cases x3 match the earlier per-member probes except job-search case 1 (7/9, the 2 misses routed to the job-hunter orchestrator; 9/9 before). v1.1.2 (2026-10-19): gate fix (bundled copy, re-synced byte-identical from resume-tailor) - verify_no_fabrication.py: a new word that starts a bare line was never a proper-noun candidate (any word after a line break was skipped as a sentence start), so a new tool added as its own line in a one-per-line list (SKILLS / Budgeting / Scheduling / Salesforce) gave verdict clean. A word that starts a line, the first line included, is now a candidate unless the text before it ends with . ! or ?; it flags only if the source has it nowhere, in any case, so a truthful reformat stays quiet. Bullet lines and mid-line words were already caught. Pre-existing gap, found while verifying the 26d7738 fix. v1.1.1 (2026-10-19): gate fix - verify_no_fabrication.py: two kinds of reformat noise. (1) A word already in the source was flagged as a new proper noun when a reformat moved it mid-line or capitalized it (one-per-line competencies joined with " | ": Budgeting, Sales, Team). Proposed proper nouns are now compared case-insensitively against every word of the source, wherever it sits. (2) A unit letter (k, M, b) took the first letter of the next word, even across a line break ("20 Mechanics" -> "20 M"), so a rewrapped line changed the token and an old number was flagged as new; the context snippet then came from the first substring match, so "20" showed the context of "200+". Units now count only when no letter follows, and context is taken from a whole-token match. "200+" was already one token. New tools, employers and numbers still flag. Found by the owner's Mode A run (2026-10-19). v1.1.0 (2026-10-18): description only. A live trigger probe (normal tool set, user hooks off, 3 samples per prompt) showed the skill loading for 1 of 9 runs of three in-domain prompts (make me sound like I know a tool, research the company before the interview, mock panel) in both a full install and a family-only install; the base model answered directly and scripted unverified experience. The new description names company research, practice answers, mock interviews and 'sounding experienced in a skill they lack', and says to load the skill rather than answer from general knowledge. Probe with the new text: 9/9, controls 3/3. Do-not-use clauses unchanged. Owner-approved 2026-10-18. v1.0.1 (2026-10-18): gate fix - verify_no_fabrication.py: a comma right after a number ("In 2023, four new") was kept as part of the token, so a number or year already in the source was flagged as new ("2023,", "40,"). Trailing commas are now stripped; inner commas ("1,200") are kept and truly new numbers are still flagged. Found by the first live outcome-eval run of interview-prep (2026-10-18). v1.0.0 (2026-10-18) adds interview-prep as the 8th job-hunter family member (idea borrowed from the ai-job-search /interview command, built on our own anti-fabrication rules). load_application.py reads one tracked application (tracker.json entry, the submitted resume and cover letter, posting text, confirmed LESSONS.md entries) without writing the tracker. build_prep_pack.py builds a stage-specific pack (6 stages) mapping posting requirements to the user's real lines, with STAR scaffolds, honest gap bridges, questions to ask, and source-checked research (posting URLs rejected, interviewer research kept professional). Every answer line is a blockquote; the claims subcommand extracts them for the bundled verify_no_fabrication gate (byte-identical to resume-tailor). Optional mock-interview mode. Never auto-sends or contacts anyone.
